findings.asked: Two banks with different rates in different years.
findings.wentWrong: The second year was the problem: the rate was applied to the original deposit (simple interest) or the two rates were added; multiplier users struggled with 0.5%.
findings.rule: Year two acts on the balance after year one; 0.5% is the multiplier 1.005.

findings.asked: A decrease followed by an increase.
findings.wentWrong: Most were right; those who misread did two decreases.
findings.rule: Read the direction of each change separately.

findings.asked: Repeated proportional change: a decrease then an increase.
findings.wentWrong: Method known by nearly all, but many carried out two decreases and got half marks.
findings.rule: Decrease then increase: multiply by (1 - a) then by (1 + b).

ruleToRemember: Multiplier = 1 plus or minus r/100; apply each change to the running total in the order given; percentage change = change / original x 100; money to 2 d.p.
aStarSignal: Choosing the multiplier method for a mixed sequence of changes and giving an exact money answer without intermediate rounding.
